tips.comment: Roger Varian continues in great form and has identified a great opportunity for his fast-improving three-year-old, Sallaal. Despite various misdemeanors before his last race at this course, he still won with a bit to spare. He will have gained invaluable experience from that and can account for his elders as he progresses again.

Sent off second favourite for the Buckingham Palace Stakes over 7 furlongs at Royal Ascot last time out but raced as if something was amiss. Possibilities of a bounce back eased 3 pounds and upped in trip.

Only 2-34, which is quite remarkable given he used to have a three-figure rating. But he's slipped down the weights lately, yet has run well the last two times in similar events at Redcar and Musselburgh. Needs a bit more, but unlikely to be far away once again this afternoon.

Sailthisshipalone looks poised to outrun his odds in this contest. He shaped with more promise than the bare result suggests when last seen. He didn't get the clearest of runs but finished off well under sympathetic handling. With a decent draw and potential to sit just off the pace in a field lacking clear front runners, he could get the right race shape to launch a late challenge.

Rogue Supremacy has run in Listed company at Royal Ascot and Sandown in his last two races and did not get a clear run in either race after winning his first race at Wetherby. Despite top weight in this nursery at Hamilton he should get a clear run with only four runners and is the most likely winner.

This is a Class 4 nursery with £5,000 to the winner, presenting an ideal opportunity for Soca Star to break through. Trained by John and Sean Quinn, who are in strong recent form with three winners over the past fortnight, Soca Star appears poised for success. Despite attracting market support in her last two starts, she's been somewhat unfortunate??'keen early and caught up in quickening pace before being overtaken late by deep closers like One Rhythm. She now enters nurseries for the first time and looks to be ahead of her opening mark. The booking of talented 5lb claimer Alex Jary adds further appeal. In a field of just four runners, she could secure a soft lead and dictate the race from the front. This marks her fifth attempt, and conditions suggest she may well open her account today.
Sire form 'Time Test' shows a whopping 55% win rate overall here at Hamilton. The horse drops 2 classes since the last run. Could well surprise here.

Plenty of runs from the 6yo mare in the last 12 months and I like the fact that her biggest defeat has only been by 3L. She has 1 win from 4 this year, beaten just 1/2L three weeks ago and posting a big RPR rating in the process. This is not a strong looking handicap, she’s a previous C/D winner and is suited by some give in the ground.
SIXCOR is running pretty true at the moment and based on the handicap run over this trip the run before last could feature once again. Well drawn and pace profile also suits.

Refuge has always liked Hamilton and goes particularly well on stiff uphill tracks. The last time he raced here, he was second to Woohoo, who was in terrific form at the time, so that rates a decent effort. His last two runs weren't as encouraging, but he's been dropped a pound in the ratings. The useful Lewis Chalkley takes off seven, and Refuge should have a fighting chance of hitting the target.

5 race maiden, who is far from straightforward, throwing away several races either by being slow away or pulling too hard. But despite his quirks, he has shown there is some decent ability lurking beneath the surface. Staying on last time out at Chelmsford despite a slow overall pace, having handled the bend poorly. Eased a pound, maybe more suitable conditions here and in a weaker race, is worth a gamble at double digits.

This race looks like it will be between the two market principals, Silent City and Brielle. The former won nicely at Windsor on her second start, although it didn't look a strong race. Brielle was second at Thirsk last time to a winner that followed up, which gives hope that it was a good effort. The selection drops considerably back in trip here, and that is odd. The point that sways me towards Brielle, though, is the jockeys booked for the pair. Silent City has a very inexperienced apprentice on board, who has yet to ride a winner, and rides Hamilton for the first time. Danny Tudhope rides Brielle, and his experience can be the deciding factor.
Three turf runs for the 6yo mare this year, getting her act together four weeks ago with a cosy 3L win. She has a higher mark now but she was rated 12lb higher last summer.
Not many Goldie horses here today, but this one had the best run to date last time. A decent third and looks like its time to strike is near. Won't mind rain and big player.

Veteran who hasn't won for some time but has posted some decent efforts off basement marks recently and ran well when 4th in a big field at Thirsk a fortnight ago. Down a lb and should go very well in this very weak race.

Now that this horse has got the winning thread, I fancy him to make it a hat trick of wins off this 4lb higher mark. He was even outpaced at a point in that previous win before running on really well. The key with that form is firstly that he showed a great attitude to get back up, and secondly that this extra furlong looks certain to suit and will play to his stamina strengths. Looks to have a huge chance and will love these conditions more than most.
Veteran, who is yet to win this season, has been running fairly consistently and wasn't beaten far when 3rd off this mark over this trip at Ayr last time. Unlikely to be far away in this poor race.

Four-time winner Come On John looks interesting on his second start for this yard. His last win was at Wolverhampton in March. He was 5th on stable debut over 1m 2f at Newcastle last month, but the step up to 1m 5f off a 1lb lower mark makes him a good each-way bet here.

Goldie and Mulreannan are here in the last and must be feared. Ok, 4th last time and although nothing to shout about in 6 runs, could easily come good. The trainer loves winning the nightcap. No surprise if this wins. Can grab some place money.
Won at Doncaster last month and followed up with a second at Haydock despite faltering at the start. Can make amends here.

Newmarket novice winner at 2 who has been lightly raced since but took a huge step forward from reappearance when 3rd in a fillies event here last month. Dropped a lb for that and this daughter of Night of Thunder should be capable of striking off this sort of mark.

Not beaten far over a mile on soft ground at Carlisle last time out 5th of 16 beat 1.75 lengths. This slight step up in trip should suit and was beaten just a neck into second place over 9 furlongs here in his penultimate race in a higher Class 3 grade.
Possibly better on AW, but worth an each-way punt here. Dropped back significantly in class and reverts back to a mile from the same mark.

This horse ran his best race for a while when dropping into a class 4 last time out, where he was making ground when hampered and not given too hard a time after that. This is clearly his level, and a mile on ground on the softer side of good is absolutely ideal. There's a first-time jockey booking too for one who does particularly well for this stable. The draw of stall 3 should also be a positive, and he looks a great e/w bet at 14/1.
Her third start of this term's campaign, and she could improve, especially if there is some give in the ground. Some rain is forecast this afternoon. She has traveled up from Yorkshire for this race.

Noble Horizon finished 2nd at Newmarket last time out to a horse with a tall reputation.
The level of his form is superior to most of his rivals here and his first win should be forthcoming.

Just three career runs from the 3yo filly. She was only 4th in a novice stakes two weeks ago, outpaced late on, not given a hard time. It was a useful looking £21K contest, the first two home in that race are rated 77+. Trained at a top yard and you could expect more improvement from her. Her opening handicap mark of 66 looks attractive.

Spartan Times barely came out of 2nd gear when hacking up 8 days ago. The selection was sent to the lead 6 furlongs out and bossed the race from there onwards. In all honesty he could have won by 10 lengths. The winning margin was deceptive to say the least, with retained jockey G Wood just hands and heels on his mount. Races off a 15lbs higher mark here....connections must feel they have plenty in hand against this lot. Already has more entries next week so potential to build up a winning sequence. 5/2 wont last long. Nap.
Sea Of Charm won at Brighton in May and last time was second of four in a handicap at Brighton. Plenty of money on this one and the conditions look good for a big run.

0-9 and has taken a while to get the hang of things but has run well in both starts so far this season, at Bath and here over 10 furlongs when only beaten half a length in a bunch finish. Very much looks ready for this step up in trip, so should be capable of breaking his duck this afternoon.

Sceptic won on the return back in March off a 57 and was not bad when last here in April, finishing fourth off a 59. Last month he was sixth at Kempton, but that was only just over 2L away from the winner when stepping up in trip to 1m3f off a 59. All of which makes me think today's 57 and 1m4f could be doable.

ROSE LIGHT looks worth an each way interest at 14/1-16/1 having run one of her best recent races over C&D on tomorrow's forecast Good to Firm when finishing 2nd of 8 in June 2024. She runs off 5lb lower here and Robdert Havlin has won on her before. For a more detailed write-up please see my X feed.

B Associates won twice for Owen last August and September at 6f but changed yards and has been pants while mainly running at 7f. But last month changed back to James Owen and a back of the pack run on AW at 5f. I am relying on getting back on turf at 6f to see a revival.

Two decent runs from the 3yo last month. He was a good 2nd of 10 three weeks ago in a similar 0-50 classified stakes, only outpaced by the winner late on - the winner who looked to be well treated at the weights in that contest. I like the fact that the rest came home in single file. Strong jockey booking, every chance.

This unexposed 3 year old has just the 4 races to her name and beaten three quarters of a length over this trip at Brighton off a pound higher mark last time out. Tom Marquand taking the ride for the first time could be a positive sign.

Three solid runs from the 3yo filly since April, 2nd of 15, 2nd of 12 and 3rd of 11. There have been a few winners coming out of those races. Same handicap mark again and this 0-55 handicap looks very weak.

Four career runs from the 3yo. A decent handicap debut two weeks ago after coming off a 7 month break and he should be better for the run. He was beaten just 2L that day in a 9 runner contest, not helping himself by hanging left at a crucial time a furlong out. He was beaten by some race fit and in form rivals. This is a much weaker handicap.

Desert Beauty has not won yet but did a grand job when second at 7f last month off a 46, missing out by just over 2L. Although fifth last time out, she was only a length and a half away from the winner at 6f and kept on to the post, which makes me think today's return to 7f could suit this improver.
Has recently been gelded. Last time out came 7th. Now making handicap debut and back up in trip. Could make an impact in a weak race.
Saffredi looks on a good handicap mark. Ran well last time at Newbury over 6 furlongs, coming 3rd of 14. This race looks easier.

Gelded son of Sixties Icon & Emtem ( Dam's sire Bungle Inthejungle ) who was last seen at Kempton 14 days ago where finishing a respectable 4th/10 closing with promise at the finish currently operating on a mark of 67 having found himself a straightforward assignment that will suit him extremely well here J A Osborne's inmate looks poised to strike here with the track here at Chepstow also very well likely to play into his strengths here jockey Saffie Osborne takes the ride and can give Em Four a promising ride here at Chepstow must be taken very seriously in a race of this nature and should have a huge role to play in this class 5 handicap over on the business end

Rating has never run well when first up after a break. She returned at the start of this month, only 3L away from the winner when fifth, having stepped up to 1 mile for the first time. It's worth an EW chance that today's 1m2f could suit now second up EW.

Bettys Tiara has finished 2nd in her last two races and now tries a longer distance for the first time. Having finished 2nd in four of her ten hurdle races after starting her racing career with a win in a bumper, she looks the likely winner.

The model I run suggests Whiskey on Ice can win this one. This result has been driven by Whiskey on Ice having the second highest RPR of the 8-horse race but is not penalized for it in the weights. All horses carry a very similar amount. Form figures look to be improving with figures of 5-534, and Paddy Handlon on board relieves a further 7 lbs around this longer 2m 7f trip, which is helpful. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Sixty Plus can win this one. Sixty Plus lines up here with a comparably high RPR but has an official ranking that looks like it's well treated off this mark. Over a stone less in weight to the top weight and looks progressive. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator due to the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

LILOO D'ORES didn't perform badly on return from lengthy break at Carlisle at the start of the season, and she's a contender if back in that sort of mood here. The subsequent runs at Uttoxeter and the Pull-up at Perth will need forgiving, but have served to significantly reduce the handicap mark.

Deal Em High's win last time was the first in 4 years, so not exactly one to rely on. King Of The Story's win over CD last time followed a promising 4th over CD. Had Henry Box Brown in 2nd, but the manner of the win doesn't suggest a reversal will be likely.

Comes into this off the back of a win last time out. With that victory coming over this course and distance. He won cosily as mentioned above last time out, on just his second chase run. He didn't get much luck in running, yet still found enough to repel the top weight runner-up, Fat Sam. He's now running off his correct mark, having run from out the weights last time. Robert Dunne is booked to ride again. He's clearly unexposed over the larger obstacles. If he runs a similar race to last time out this time, he should go close again here.
Unexposed is better than bare form. 4th last time out, which was an improvement, and has been well backed in a weak-looking race.

The model I run suggests Kopa Kilana can win this one. This result has been driven by Kopa Kilana having the highest RPR of this smaller 5-horse race but has the lowest official ranking. This subsequently means Kopa Kilana steps out carrying the lowest amount of weight around this 2m round trip. Champion jockey Sean Bowen picks up the reins for this trip. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Kopa Kilana is short considering no wins in 21 hurdle races. That doesn't inspire much, even though this is a stable debut for Olly Murphy, who can improve pretty much any horse. EZ Tiger is next in the betting but has figures of 312-1. The last win followed a break, and he had a previous winner behind. That seems more sensible.

First two chase starts have been good and will have no issue with conditions. Looks sure to give his running, whereas the other two will have to improve markedly on anything they have produced recently.

Paddy De Pole goes for his first chase under rules, having previously run and won in points. He should soon leave his hurdle mark behind over fences, and this three-horse handicap chase at Worcester looks like a good opportunity for a winning start.

The model I run suggests Davidoc can win this one. This result has been driven by Davidoc having the highest RPR of this very small 3-runner field. Davidoc has the lowest official ranking, which means he steps out carrying the lowest amount of weight around this 2m 7f handicap chase. Carries over a stone less than the top weight and current market favorite. The model has issued a moderate stake indicator, which translates to a 1pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Radharc Na Slaine can win this one. This result has been driven by Radharc Na Slaine having a comparably high RPR but an official ranking that leaves running off an attractive mark. Nearly 2 stone gap in weight differential to the top weight and has shown some reasonable improvement in form coming into this. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Boskill Borden can win this one. This result has been driven by Boskill Borden lining up here with the highest RPR of this 9-horse field. Boskill Borden is not overly penalized for it in the weights, and Shane Fenelon takes off a further 5 lbs, which can be helpful over this 2m4f trip. Last out only 10 days ago and looks to be in improving form. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Has transferred back to his first trainer, Fergal O'Brien. Now down to a career-low mark. He comes into this in poor form, admittedly. Hopes are pinned on the change of scenery and career-low mark sparking an improved effort this time. His sole career win over hurdles came over this course and distance off a 5 lbs higher mark, giving 17 lbs in weight to the runner-up, Eaton Lady, by 3/4 length. Finding plenty for pressure. He's struggled for form since then. He did try his hand at chasing, however. Hopefully, the change in yard, the short break, and the return to a track he's had success at in the past can spark a return to form.

I'm happy to put a line through The Flying Poet's last run at Perth. I don't think the tight track suited, and Worcester, despite its easy finish, is more of a galloping track. Olly Murphy's 6-year-old is lightly raced and unexposed as a stayer. I wouldn't be surprised if a punt is in the offing.

The model I run suggests Palm Beach can win this one. Palm Beach lines up with the highest RPR of the 12-runner race but has the second lowest official ranking. This leaves Palm Beach carrying what is essentially the lowest weight around this longer 2m 7f trip. Elliot England picks up the reins and takes off a further 10 lbs, which takes the weight gap to the top weight to be a total of over 2 stone. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Indian Sunbird won over course and distance last July and returned to form with a win at Southwell on his last start in May. The runner-up there won next time out, and up 5 lbs, he looks a good EW bet with 4 places on offer.

Stripe Of Honour, 12yo, looks in some of his best form judged on the last two starts, both times from out of the handicap, claiming two 3rd place finishes. (He's 1lb out today.) The CD winner's last run was just ten days ago over CD, and he stayed on well late, well clear of the rest. If he gives his running today, his rivals will need to be at their very best to hold him off.
Won with plenty in hand at York in an apprentice handicap over 1m4f and should be competitive here in a ladies' race with Lauren Frost aboard. Runs off the same handicap mark of 70 and can follow up.

The 5yo was a hurdle winner four weeks ago and in good shape. He was a Class 4 AW handicap winner on the flat during January and runs off a similar mark for this Class 5 turf handicap. Strong jockey booking for this amateur female riders’ handicap.
Ella Smart rides Will, and here she combines with the Moores on a useful horse who should be well suited here. Kotari looks set to go close at around 4/1 odds.

A good amateur rider in Heidi Palin combined with a good trainer in Ian Williams on a horse who ran an improver's race last time out. Looks set to go well at decent each-way odds and I see some value in an open lineup.

Arrives here in good form winning last 2 at Salisbury & Brighton both over today's 7f trip & on good to firm . The other win in 11 race career came here over CD on good / good to soft back in August 2023 and not all horses perform on this undulating track so the CD win is a bonus .

MAFNOOD looks way too big with Ladbrokes at 13/2 compared to the 4/1 on offer with Bet365. This horse was 8lb 'wrong' with the winner when he was given too much to do last time out over course and distance fifteen days ago. Given a better ride, he should be hard to keep out of the frame.

Future Cutlet is an interesting runner here. He has firmish ground for the first time since his debut on June 24, where he didn't run too badly in a Limerick maiden. His last race at Goodwood was well contested, and he was dropped out and then penned in. If he can handle the firmer ground, he must have a fair shout.

The 4-year-old has run well in his three races this year. He was a good 3rd at this track two weeks ago, outpaced in the last 100 yards, but he was still 4 lengths clear of the rest. The form looks solid with the winner running a nice race since. This shorter trip should suit him. Same good apprentice in the saddle, and he should have a better feel for this runner and this tricky Epsom track.

Platinum Prince won at Goodwood last month in a C5 but could not follow up when last out at the same venue off the same mark but in a C4. I think getting back to C5 today and up 3 lbs with a 7 lbs claimer could see him bounce back, with today's expected rain likely to help as well. EW

This M Beckett-trained colt has finished second in his first two races over six furlongs on soft ground at Goodwood and the latest over seven furlongs on good to firm ground at Salisbury 22 days ago. When keeping on well in the closing stages, he was beaten 1 3/4 lengths behind the D Menuisier-trained Goodwood Galaxy. With Rossa Ryan booked to ride, he can make it third time lucky today.
Won from this mark over course and distance a year ago and comes here in form. With Billy the Kid on top for the first time, it is a strong bet here.

Despite being beaten in all her starts, she's shaping up nicely and made a good impression on the turf, which she returns to today. She will appreciate the step back up and handicap debut into class 6 company after racing in 4 & 5. This should be a modest level. The jockey and trainer both hold good records for this course.
Form of his second last time is of the highest level, beating the third home by 4 lengths, with that one running third in the Derby next time. Strong win bet here.

Galen is back in Ireland after running overseas. Back with a bang when second in the Wolferton Stakes at Royal Ascot in a quality race for merely listed company. Has to concede weight to the field for pattern win penalties. Good chance here.
Purview may have many claims for this, but the selection can give it much work. Snellen has been runner-up of 23 in its last start - class 2 at Ascot a month ago.

This J P Murtagh-trained 3-year-old filly made a promising racecourse debut over one mile and one furlong on soft ground at Gowran Park 32 days ago. She was beaten by 3 1/4 lengths in second of the eight runners behind the H De Bromhead-trained Offshore Bay. With improvement expected and B M Coen in the saddle, she can go one place better today.

Heiselectric can be expected to be very competitive in its debut today, as relations enable us to predict. It will not be easy, but possible that it lags behind or is close to the favorite, Walk The Highline, that made a promising debut a month ago.

Fairy Oak has been contesting vastly superior races to this one, including a 3 lengths fifth to Venetian Sun in the Albany at Royal Ascot. The extra distance here will help her finishing kick. Big chance.

Yellowstone Lake is a 2yo filly trained by P Twomey, making her debut for owners Zinlo Syndicate. She is out of an unraced dam related to some smart sorts who posted personal best RPR of 102-105-121. Trading Leather, who won the Irish Derby, is one of them. The owners ( have had two pattern winners with K J Condon; Marvadar 104 and Straight Of Zanzibar 103 ) have had two horses with Twomey since 2023. Purple Lily won on her 2yo debut (run once as a 2yo), then made a winning debut as a 3yo and is rated 107. Then there is City Of Memphis, who won on 2yo debut in 2024 and is rated 106. Yellowstone Lake could follow in the same footsteps and is likely to be above average. She is my short-priced banker of the day.

Real Encounter is a newcomer to watch in this maiden race at Leopardstown. Though unraced, she carries the appeal of a well-bred juvenile who's likely to improve significantly with experience. Debutants often benefit from a learning run. Her trainer/jockey combination looks capable and deliberate. While the market may understandably be cautious, her profile suggests a smart, unexposed type who's worth the risk given the price.
Third to two subsequent winners at Leopardstown in June and was then runner-up at Killarney on Monday. Can go one better here with the help of first time cheekpieces.

Clonmacash has yet to win on turf after 16 attempts, but this 3-time winner at Dundalk has been placed in his last 3 turf starts. 4th in two course and distance handicaps in June, he finished 3rd at Fairyhouse last week. He looks sure to go well again and is a good each-way bet with 4 places on offer.
Not hot last season's form yet, but came good this time last year. Off a good mark today and gets a good draw. Trip looks ideal, can run a place.
Run Forrest Run has been another horse who has probably been in my notes for far too long, but the erratic 7-y-o could be in with an e.w. chance if turned out to do so.

Pinball Wizard put in a much improved effort when 6th of 16 last time out on just his third start for his new trainer and could go even closer now with a stronger pace, decent draw and the stable doing better than they have at any stage of the season. I also think the jockey is good value for her 4lb claim in this Apprentice race and she has a better record at the track than most of these. The trainer has had 3 wins and 2 places from his last 11 runners and this horse has been dropped a generous 2lb after that effort last time out so I don't see why he can't be involved in the finish here.

The model I run suggests Galileo Sand can win this one. Galileo Sand lines up here with the highest RPR of this limited experience national hunt flat. Galileo Sand is not penalized for it in the weights and goes out carrying largely the same amount as every other horse. Second when last out 67 days ago, and if near that kind of form, can go close again coming back from a small break. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
No comment made
Brought up the HT and goes for the 4-timer here. She will be running in better races than this before long, and this is a confident bet with connections putting up a 7lb claimer to negate penalties.

The model I run suggests Kilbuny Supersonic can win this one. Kilbuny Supersonic lines up here with a comparably high RPR but has an official ranking that leaves him looking well treated off this mark. All horses carry a very similar amount around this 2m 4f trip. Pat O'Brien relieves a further 7 lbs and form figures look good. Figures are 3161, with that last victory coming 61 days ago. Coming back from a short break here and needs to run well fresh. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
100,000 guineas yearling from the in-form Donnacha O'B yard, whose youngsters are in top form. Wootton Bassett filly on racecourse debut can go well first time up.

Sherekiya makes her debut in what looks like a winnable fillies' maiden, and there's reason to expect a positive showing first time out. She's bred to stay a mile well and represents connections who have a respectable record with debutantes, especially when pitched into this sort of company. While she'll learn plenty from the experience, the setup suggests she's here to run - not just gain fitness. One of the more interesting newcomers.

Followed up last time and is whacked up 11 lb for hat-trick bid, but he won that race very easily. The runner-up won next time out with the third home also winning a subsequent race. Worth backing here.

Just 4th start for the Cromwell team and ran well on debut for the stable when qualifying for this when 2nd @Downpatrick after travelling powerfully. Just 3lbs higher here and has won on the flat in the meantime and also come 2nd to recent hurdle winner Billie Frechette. Has a nice weight.

Boston Rajj won at Sligo in June off a mark of 105 and has run well off higher marks since at shorter trips. His win was his only attempt at 3 miles, and he was just beaten for pace when dropping back to 2m 2f at Downpatrick 5 days later off a 9 lbs higher mark. He finished 4th, beaten 3 lengths at Kilbeggan last week over 2m 3f, but the step up to an extended 2m 4f on rain-softened ground looks ideal, and he looks like a good EW bet with 5 places on offer.

The paper favorite will take some stopping, but one I put up recently, coming third in the end, clattered 2 out and got knocked back, is Folley Beach. It now gets 13 lb from its conqueror, so it looks a tidy each way. Ran a good fourth at this meeting last year, so knows its way.

Probably overpriced at 20s. Placed from a pound lower on seasonal reappearance on penultimate start. Disappointed last time, but if in the same form as reappearance run, then has a chance of finishing top 5.

Hills Of Glory is just the type to upset at big odds here after a penultimate start win at Downpatrick and then a useful sixth at his last appearance. Gavin Cromwell has him racing well and the horse would not need to improve much in an open field to take the thick end of the purse.

The model I ran suggests Way Down South can cause an upset and win this one. Way Down South lines up here with the highest RPR of this larger 16-horse field and has an official ranking that is third bottom. This leaves him stepping out carrying the third lowest amount of weight around this 2m 4f trip. 9th when last out but needed the run after a break. Turned around quickly 14 days later to go out and improve. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Thrown in at the deep end on handicap debut last time, finishing mid-division in the Sandringham at Royal Ascot. This is a much easier race and races over a furlong further here, which seems sure to suit.
The selection makes more appeal at these odds than the favorite, Esherann, which is making its handicap debut. A fortnight ago, Onemoredance got, at this distance, its second win in four races .

The model I run suggests Palpatate can win this one. Palpatate lines up here with the highest RPR of this 7-runner field. Steps out carrying the joint lowest weight around this 2m 1f National Hunt flat. The jockey on board is claiming a further 7 lbs relief, and this could be the difference. Smaller 7-horse field here with some running for the first time. Palpatate has plenty of experience under his belt from prior races and can get this one over the line first. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

An each-way chance is taken with Texas Red, who ran a bit too green on debut in another Ladies NH Flat race. The winner of that was a Willie Mullins 1/2 favorite who left the field behind. But taking the finishing distances into consideration, I thought the horse did quite well because three of the five who finished ahead were very well fancied.
Tatum has been very consistent since moving to lengths like today's in its last 4 races, including a win at this course.

The model I run suggests Tippawan Haa can cause an upset and win this one. Tippawan Haa lines up here with a comparably high RPR but looks well treated in the weights. John Shinick takes off 3 lbs further for claiming, having only run one race before and came 6th. If the progressive type can put in a good performance here 31 days later, the model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Usually ridden positively, was held up last time, his first run for more than 5 months and will certainly come on for that run. Drops back in trip here and will set off to make all. Should go close.

The model I run suggests Give Him A Chance should win this one. Give Him A Chance lines up here with a comparably high RPR in this larger 16-horse race. Is not penalized for it in the weights and has shown some glimpses of form. Winner last time out and looks to repeat that over this 2m 4f trip. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Five-time winner Swelltime looks interesting here following his improved run at Wexford when he was 5th of 14. That was his first sign of any form since winning over course and distance in August last year. That was off a mark of 100, but he was given an 8 lbs rise for that win, which saw him unplaced in 6 subsequent starts, though he was back down to 100 at Wexford. The handicapper is giving him a chance as he is down another 4 lbs and looks like a good EW bet with 5 places on offer.
Good each-way bet here. Dropping down the rankings to a very much challenging mark now, and at these odds, certainly a good shout for an each-way bet

I like the look of VINTAGE GOLD here. He’s had 3 runs this term and might be ready to leave some of that old form behind. His ‘good’ ground form isn’t great, but everything on ‘yielding’ and below reads much better. He’s a C/D winner as he won here last year on yielding to soft and landed a punt for connections 25/1-17/2. Joe Murphy loves this place and has his string in red hot form right now, 2 winners and 3 places from 7 on the week. He’s 1lb below his winning mark and the booking of up-and-coming conditional rider Eoin Staples adds another layer of confidence. I thought the forecast 12/1 was ok, I’m very surprised at 22/1.

The Banger Doyle failed again to win a hurdle race when 2nd at Tipperary last time. He has been pushed up another two pounds, but he remains well in on his chase form, for which his mark is 29 pounds higher. Despite this looking like a more competitive handicap, he may finally break his duck over hurdles.

A tricky little handicap where Miss Maxfort looks to have a bit of scope and ran well after a break at Tipperary last time out. She looks set to go well here off the same mark with optimum conditions, and 18/1 looks a big price.

Game Phoenix has shown well so far in limited hurdles outings with a couple of runner-up finishes as well as a 3rd in just 6 previous attempts. This race looks wide open and could go one better than the recent 2nd in Cork, where it looked to have plenty in the tank when chasing down the winner. This is over a longer distance, so it could suit well.

The model I run suggests Star Official can win this one. Star Official lines up here with the highest RPR of this field and ran a good race last time out when 4th. The jockey on board is claiming and takes off a further 7 lbs, which helps over this 2m 1f trip. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

At Current odds of 40/1 I cant let Eugene O'Sullivan's 4 year old British Gelding METEOR STORM pass me by as he makes his handicap Bow. This Son of ZOUZTAR has steadily improved without setting the world on fire with his run at Cork in April a HUGE improvement as he finished 6th (of 15) a whopping 80 ok lengths better off than his penultimate (at Limerick). If we go off that last run then the forecast rain & another sharp track certainly won't do this British lad any harm. The booking of Jockey Sean O'Keefe is a big plus with his 45% place strike rate the past month. Racing off bottom weight here I'm happy to have a very small piece of the pie with 5 places on offer hitting the Frame wouldn't be a forlorn hope especially if he continues to make steady progress. Hidden in plain sight ? Possibly.
